intro: The Lenches sit on a ridge above the Vale of Evesham, with woods, field paths and the Wychavon Way linking the villages. Routes below link to their publishers, who keep the directions up to date.

walks.name: Circuit of the Lenches
walks.text: Farmland, woodland and the villages of Church Lench, Atch Lench and Rous Lench. Mostly good paths and tracks, with few stiles.

walks.name: Yeald Wood and Rous Lench
walks.text: Along the Wychavon Way between Yeald Wood and Old Yew Hill Wood to Rous Lench church, and back.

walks.name: Rous, Atch, Sheriffs and Church Lench
walks.text: Past Rous Lench Court to Atch Lench and Sheriffs Lench, then back along the Wychavon Way, with views of the Malvern Hills from the ridge.

wychavonWay.text: A waymarked 40-mile path from Droitwich Spa to Broadway, passing through Rous Lench, Church Lench and Sheriffs Lench. Locally it follows a fenced woodland path between Yeald Wood and Old Yew Hill Wood for about a mile.
wychavonWay.guide: The walkers’ guide is £5 plus postage from the county countryside team.

info.title: Maps
info.html: OS Explorer 205 (Stratford-upon-Avon & Evesham) shows every footpath and bridleway. The county’s rights of way map is on its report a path page.

info.title: Walk with a group
info.html: Evesham Ramblers and Worcester Ramblers both lead walks around the Lenches. See ramblers.org.uk for upcoming walks.

info.title: Countryside Code
info.html: Leave gates as you find them, keep dogs on a lead near livestock, and take litter home. Read the code.

report.text: Worcestershire County Council looks after public rights of way. Drop a pin on its map to report a blocked path, broken stile or gate, or a missing sign.
